# Hydra

> A Rust CLI that runs coding-agent CLIs (claude, cursor-agent, agy) in isolated git worktrees behind a deny-by-default policy, and records every run as one JSONL file whose outcome is derived from what the tools did, not from the vendor's exit code.

Use it when you need agent runs that are gated, recorded and reviewable. Do not use it as a low-latency subagent: each run is a full launch in a fresh worktree with a human-typed cleanup.

- Install: `cargo build --release`; the binary is `target/release/hydra`. macOS only. Needs a vendor CLI logged in.
- Minimal run: `hydra run --provider claude --policy standard --task "..."` prints a JSON projection and writes `~/hydra/runs/<uuidv7>.jsonl`.
- Read a run: `hydra show <prefix> [--events]`. Clean up: `hydra reap <prefix>`.
- Delegate from Claude Code: register `hydra delegate-face` as an MCP server; it exposes `delegate(provider, task, files?, policy?)`.
- Policies: judge, curate, read-only, standard, permissive, in `policies/*.json`.
- Read first: README.md, CLAUDE.md, IMPLEMENTATION.md (every departure from the design). Design: docs/harness-spec.md, docs/run-record-contract.md, docs/rungs-spec.md.
- Honest limits: the gate refuses commands naming protected paths but does not interpret shell; no container; network not cut; Linux untested.
